entities.summary:
Skilurus, a renowned Scythian king, ruled from the 2nd century BC to an unknown date. His realm encompassed the lower reaches of the Borysthenes and Hypanis rivers, as well as the northern part of Crimea, where his capital, Scythian Neapolis, was situated. Skilurus played a significant role in the ancient world, contributing to the cultural and political landscape of the region.

Skilurus's reign was marked by several key events, including the expansion of his kingdom and the establishment of trade routes with neighboring civilizations. His legacy can be seen in the many archaeological sites and artifacts that remain from his time, providing valuable insights into the lives of the ancient Scythians.

The impact of Skilurus's rule can still be felt today, with his kingdom's influence extending across the ancient world. His legacy serves as a reminder of the importance of understanding the complex web of historical events and the lasting effects they have on our world.

The Scythian king's life and reign remain shrouded in mystery, with many details unknown or lost to history. Despite this, his significance as a major figure in ancient Scythian history cannot be overstated.
